enforced_dimensions.max_input_bytes: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced on both path.stat().st_size (before reading) and len(data) (for bytes/stream sources)
enforced_dimensions.max_output_bytes: codec/writer/writer.py -- enforced on the final encoded byte length
enforced_dimensions.max_xml_nodes: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced incrementally during element parsing, not only after full materialization
enforced_dimensions.max_nesting_depth: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced incrementally during element parsing
enforced_dimensions.max_entries: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced per-element on attribute_count (an attribute flood on a single element is rejected even if total node/depth limits are not exceeded)
enforced_dimensions.max_decompressed_bytes: codec/reader/reader.py -- enforced on cumulative decoded text_bytes across the document

not_applicable_dimensions.max_header_bytes: no fixed-size binary header in this format (well-formed XML text)
not_applicable_dimensions.max_compression_ratio: no compression in XLIFF's own XML serialization

evidence.key_proof: test_an_attribute_flood_on_one_element_is_rejected and test_a_text_flood_exceeding_the_decoded_byte_limit_is_rejected both prove max_entries/max_decompressed_bytes enforcement happens incrementally during parsing, not after the full document is already materialized; test_a_wide_shallow_document_is_bounded_by_node_count_not_depth proves max_xml_nodes and max_nesting_depth are independent dimensions, not one masking the other; test_default_limits_apply_without_caller_opt_in proves XLIFF_DEFAULT_LIMITS is the enforced floor even when a caller passes no explicit limits.
